body:
DESIGNED WITH MYK IN CHAT, 2026-08-18. This ticket OPENS AT THE DESIGN STAGE: the working spec is
the deliverable, and no implementation code is written until Myk's word in chat.

WHY THIS EXISTS. A session on 2026-08-18 drove real federation between two stores with DIFFERENT
operator keys. Deltas federate; law does not. Bob pulled all 7 of alice's deltas, then his store
answered "nothing is registered: the gateway has no queryable surface yet ... foreign law is inert on
a governed store". That is correct per SPEC 28 and it is the single most confusing thing a new peer
meets. The only workaround today is for the receiver to register their own equivalent schema, which
makes them the author of law they did not write.

WHAT IS ALREADY BUILT, and it is more than expected:
- The inbox mechanism (SPEC 39.3). A container declaration carrying an `inboxOf` pointer is a nested
  container with its OWN GROUND; `containerScope` gathers every active pool marking the parent. The
  gather is a LOOP, so one parent supports MANY inboxes (container.ts, the addGather loop).
- Blessing. `Gateway.adoptLaw` and `Gateway.blessAll` are real, tested, and idempotent BY
  CONSTRUCTION: an adoption record inherits the manifest row's timestamp, so re-running re-mints the
  same delta id and a standing strike still covers it. A polling loop cannot un-curse what was
  cursed, and cannot append narrative forever.
- Un-blessing (Myk's "curse"). A strike on the adoption record, durable across re-runs by the same
  timestamp inheritance.
- Receiver-chosen naming. `livingNameOf` is `opts.as ?? ex.lensName`, and `schemaLawAddress`
  DELIBERATELY EXCLUDES the lens name from law identity. So a name never travels; law travels as a
  content address and the receiver names it.
- `drop()` purges every store beneath a container and refuses by name if a byte survives.

WHAT IS MISSING:
- Nothing in production publishes a manifest row. `isManifestRow` is minted only in tests, so
  `blessAll` has nothing to enumerate for an ordinary registration. THE CONTAINER-TO-CONTAINER SHAPE
  DISSOLVES THIS: the outbox container's membership IS the manifest.
- `pull` knows nothing of containers (zero hits for "container" in src/federation/pull.ts).
- There is no channel record, no standing instruction, and no CLI for blessing.

THE DESIGN, as settled with Myk:
1. Federation is CONTAINER-TO-CONTAINER. A publisher offers a container. A receiver names a container
   to receive it. ONE-WAY only for now; two-way is a future feature and is deliberately out of scope.
2. Both directions of initiation are supported: a publisher sends a federation request, OR a receiver
   subscribes to an available source. Vetting of a public aggregator is explicitly NOT overthought
   here.
3. The receiver names one container. Underneath, EACH CHANNEL GETS ITS OWN NESTED POOL inside it.
   That is what makes severing one peer a proven `drop()` rather than a filtered delete by author,
   and it keeps foreign bytes out of the receiver's primary ground by construction.
4. THE RECEIVER ASSIGNS THE NAMESPACE PREFIX, not the publisher. This closes the squatting hazard
   accounts.ts already documents: the GraphQL door maps every non-alphanumeric to `_`, so `x:Foo` and
   `x_Foo` both serve at `x_Foo`. Because the receiver assigns every prefix, injectivity is LOCALLY
   CHECKABLE and a colliding prefix is refused AT ASSIGNMENT TIME, when a person can pick another.
5. Depth does not accumulate. Alice's local name for Bob's law is a fact about her store only. What
   travels is the law's address. So `alice_bob_Post` never arises.
6. The bare name is ALWAYS AN EXPLICIT ALIAS, never inferred from cardinality. On first arrival, if a
   name is unbound, the channel binds it and RECORDS that it did. A binding that emerged from set
   membership would silently change meaning when the set changed.
7. TWO ORTHOGONAL TOGGLES per channel: receiving (freeze) and blessing. Pausing blessing stops NEW
   law binding and leaves bound law working. Cursing retires ONE already-bound law. Dropping the
   inbox is a separate, permanent, destructive act.
8. Channel state is DELTAS like everything else, including a visible `last synced` value. A channel
   that quietly stopped must be distinguishable from a peer with nothing new (H9).
9. Transport stays BEHIND the container contract. Polling now; push later changes nothing above it.

OPEN, and answered as recommendations in the working spec for Myk to redline:
- Whether auto-bless defaults differently for an accepted offer versus a subscribe.
- What the channel report shows when a peer is unreachable.
- That a curse does NOT cover a republished law at a new address, which is correct and must be
  visible rather than surprising.

TIER: MYK'S MERGE. This changes what the system promises — a peer's law gains force in a receiver's
container under a standing instruction. That is a widened trust surface, and design-stage sections
are his merge regardless.
title: Federation is container-to-container — a channel, a nested inbox, and blessing on arrival
